title: On the Infinite Width and Depth Limits of Predictive Coding Networks
claim: Gradient alignment between the local-update method and backpropagation approaches perfect agreement as width grows relative to depth, throughout training.
layout: 3 heatmap panels left-to-right by training step, shared depth-width axes
description: Three side-by-side heatmaps show training steps t=0, t=50 and t=100. In each, the x-axis is network width N (2 to 2048, log-spaced) and the y-axis is depth L (2 to 32). Each cell is colored by the cosine similarity between the predictive-coding equilibrium energy gradient and the backpropagation loss gradient, using a viridis colorbar from 0 (yellow) to 1 (dark purple). The bottom-right region, with large width and small depth, is uniformly dark purple, meaning near-perfect alignment. The top-left region, with small width and large depth, is green to yellow, meaning poor alignment. The low-alignment region grows slightly as training progresses. A vertical colorbar with a cosine-similarity label sits beside the first two panels and the last one. The eye goes to the sharp color gradient along the diagonal.
caption: PC shows perfect gradient alignment with BP for vanishing depth-to-width ratios ($L/N\to0$), under stable and feature-learning parameterisations of linear residual networks. We trained linear residual networks on CIFAR-10 with the mean-field parameterisation (as defined in Table [ref]) and depth scaling exponent $\alpha=1/2$ (\S[ref]). Plotted are the cosine similarities averaged over 3 random runs between the equilibrated energy (Eq. [ref]) gradients (PC) and the MSE loss (Eq. [ref]) gradients (BP) at different training steps $t$. See \S[ref] for more details and Figure [ref] for similar results on Fashion-MNIST.
abstract: Predictive coding (PC) is a biologically plausible alternative to standard backpropagation (BP) that minimises an energy function with respect to network activities before updating weights. Recent work has improved the training stability of deep PC networks (PCNs) by leveraging some BP-inspired reparameterisations, but the scalability and theoretical basis of these methods remain unclear. To address this gap, we study the infinite width and depth limits of PCNs. For linear networks, we derive stable and "non-lazy" parameterisations when scaling both the model width and depth, revealing that the output of standard PCNs explodes with width during training. Moreover, under stable parameterisations, we show that the gradients computed by PC at activity equilibrium converge to the BP gradients for networks that are much wider than deep ($depth/width\to0$). Experiments show high gradient alignment between PC and BP at large width for different nonlinear models, including convolutional networks and transformers. Overall, this work constrains the parameterisations that are scalable with PC, while suggesting how BP could be implemented using only local updates in much wider than deep networks like the brain.
